newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president's defence adviser Milewski dies.
newsitem.headline: Polish president's defence adviser Milewski dies.

text.p: Jerzy Milewski, a top aide to Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski on defence matters and a senior member of the pre-1989 Solidarity union, died on Tuesday, the president's office said in a statement.

Milewski, who was 61, had been head of the presidential National Security Bureau, dealing with defence, for about a year. He was among only a handful of prominent figures rooted in Solidarity to accept high office from the ruling ex-communists.
The laser scientist was an active member of the Solidarity union when it first emerged at the Gdansk shipyard to become the Soviet bloc's first free trade union in 1980.
He was abroad when communist authorities declared martial law in 1981 to crush Solidarity and for eight years he ran a Brussels office coordinating the union's activities from outside Poland.

After the 1989 fall of communism he returned to Poland and in 1991 became head of the National Security Bureau under then president Lech Walesa. He then moved to the post of deputy defence minister and briefly acted as minister from 1994 to 1995.
He was caught in a dispute over the best form of civilian control over the military, which pitted former Solidarity chief Walesa against the ex-communists in government.

Milewski took the opposite line to Walesa, quit and then accepted his final post from Kwasniewski after the ex-communist beat Walesa in November 1995 elections. There he helped to formulate Polish strategy in the approach to NATO entry.
The presidential office did not reveal the cause of his death.
